meta.title: New Words at the Fair
meta.textType: dialogue: new words from a set

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to the school fair with Teacher Kim. The hall had two parts: a food side and a clothes side. Lily, Mia, Leo, and May stopped in front of a big board on the food side. It said, "GRILLED CHICKEN, GREEN CURRY, TOAST WITH CHILI JAM."

"I know chicken, but I do not know grilled," said Lily. "What does it mean?" "Look at the cook," said May. "He puts the chicken over a hot fire, and the chicken becomes brown." "Then grilled means cooked over a fire," said Lily. "Yes, and a dish with grilled chicken often smells very good," said May. "What is curry?" asked Mia. "It is a dish with a sauce, and you eat it with rice," said Leo. "Is it hot?" asked Mia. "Some curry is hot, and some is not," said Leo.

Leo bought a piece of toast with chili jam. "Toast is bread that you make brown and dry," he said. "And chili is a small red plant with a very hot taste." "How do you know that?" asked Mia. Leo ate a big piece, and his face became red. "Now I know very well," he said, and he drank a lot of water. "The jam is delicious, but the chili is too hot."

On the clothes side, a poster said, "FASHION SHOW AT ELEVEN O'CLOCK." "What is fashion?" asked Lily. "Fashion is the kind of clothes that many people like now," said May. "Look at the stage, and you can see the new clothes." A tall girl walked on the stage in a long blue skirt. She wore a silver necklace, and the necklace was a chain of small rings. "Can you describe a chain?" asked Teacher Kim. "It is many small rings that join together," said Mia. "A necklace can be a chain," said Lily, "and a bike has a chain, too."

Teacher Kim smiled and showed them a good way to learn. "When you see a new word, think about its set," she said. "Grilled, curry, toast, and chili are food words." "Fashion, chain, and ring are clothes words." "The words that you know can help you with the new ones." Lily opened her notebook and wrote two lists with the new words. She wrote food above one list and clothes above the other.

sentences.text: On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to the school fair with Teacher Kim.
The hall had two parts: a food side and a clothes side.
Lily, Mia, Leo, and May stopped in front of a big board on the food side.
It said, "GRILLED CHICKEN, GREEN CURRY, TOAST WITH CHILI JAM."
"I know chicken, but I do not know grilled," said Lily.
"What does it mean?"
"Look at the cook," said May.
"He puts the chicken over a hot fire, and the chicken becomes brown."
"Then grilled means cooked over a fire," said Lily.
"Yes, and a dish with grilled chicken often smells very good," said May.
"What is curry?" asked Mia.
"It is a dish with a sauce, and you eat it with rice," said Leo.
"Is it hot?" asked Mia.
"Some curry is hot, and some is not," said Leo.
Leo bought a piece of toast with chili jam.
"Toast is bread that you make brown and dry," he said.
"And chili is a small red plant with a very hot taste."
"How do you know that?" asked Mia.
Leo ate a big piece, and his face became red.
"Now I know very well," he said, and he drank a lot of water.
"The jam is delicious, but the chili is too hot."
On the clothes side, a poster said, "FASHION SHOW AT ELEVEN O'CLOCK."
"What is fashion?" asked Lily.
"Fashion is the kind of clothes that many people like now," said May.
"Look at the stage, and you can see the new clothes."
A tall girl walked on the stage in a long blue skirt.
She wore a silver necklace, and the necklace was a chain of small rings.
"Can you describe a chain?" asked Teacher Kim.
"It is many small rings that join together," said Mia.
"A necklace can be a chain," said Lily, "and a bike has a chain, too."
Teacher Kim smiled and showed them a good way to learn.
"When you see a new word, think about its set," she said.
"Grilled, curry, toast, and chili are food words."
"Fashion, chain, and ring are clothes words."
"The words that you know can help you with the new ones."
Lily opened her notebook and wrote two lists with the new words.
She wrote food above one list and clothes above the other.
